2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that Opposite-party No.1 as plaintiff instituted a suit praying for permanent intimation restraining the defendants from not to make any pucca house forcibly over the road as described in the 2nd schedule of the land of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the proforma defendant No. 5 is the owner of the 1st schedule land and 2nd schedule land is within the 1st schedule land. In the last settlement operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet on behalf of the government in Khatian No.1 as road within the knowledge of all concerned including the predecessor of the defendants and still the record remains as it was and in the settlement Map it was also mentioned as road. The homestead of the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 is situated in the settlement plot No. 1408, 1409, 1410 and 1411 and the homestead of plaintiff No. 4 is situated in the plot Nos. 1432, 1433, 1434 and 1436. The plaintiffs have been residing over those plots from the time of their predecessor and they used to ingress and egress from their homestead towards west over plot No.1419 as described in the 1st schedule land as road and then towards west over plot No.1479 which is the road of local Board and then used to proceed towards C & B road. Apart from that the plaintiffs and villagers by using the road under suit plot No.1419 used to go to their agricultural land with their cattle's. The defendant Nos.1-4 on 06.04.2002 gathered brick, sand, stones etc. near the suit road over plot No.1418 with a view to make a pucca house by force and as it was protested by the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 1 on 07.01.2002 by threatening plaintiff No.1 said that if anybody create any obstruction there will be murdered which gave rise the cause of action of the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegation made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that homestead plot No.1418 was recorded in the name of their father Habibur Rahman Chowdhury and after his death the defendant Nos.1-4 became owner and possessor of the said land by constructing houses therein. Habibur Rahman Chowdhury in his life time purchased the entire land of plot No.1417 and had been possessing the same. In the east of plot No.1418 Reasot Ali was the recorded owner, of .40 acre land under plot No.1411 who sold out .30 acres of land in favour of Sarafat Ali Chowdhury sister's husband of the answering defendants vide registered deed dated 01.07.1962 and delivered possession. Subsequently, Reasot Ali while sold out .10 acres of land in favour of plaintiff No. 1 Abdul Kadir Chowdhury, the brother-in-law (sister's husband) of answering defendant Sorafat Ali Chowdhury by filing preemption Case No.43 of 1984 got an order of preemption which has been upheld up to the higher court. Sorafot Ali Chowdhury acquired .40 acres of land by way of purchase and preemption and since then the plaintiff No.1 out of grudge trying to cause loss and harass to the answering defendants and apart from that the father of plaintiff was borgadar under the defendants. The road contiguous south to the homestead of defendants and towards east-west although owned by the predecessor of the defendants in the last settlement operation it was recorded in the government khas khatian No.1 over plot No.1419, area .20 acres and west end of that road which has been connected with the road of local board over plot no.1409 and as the said road has been recorded as gupat the defendants had been using the same from the time of their predecessor. The defendants by removing their ancient tin shed house constructed pucca residential house before filing this suit and in the south boundary raised a pucca boundary wall in their demarcated boundary. Both, plaintiffs and defendants entered into an amicable settlement regarding the suit road and on 12.08.1988 the arbitrator gave an award which has been registered but the plaintiff No.1 after long time of that judgment filed Title Suit No.366 of 1989 relying on some false statement which has subsequently withdrawn and then filed Misc. Case No. 30 of 1993 for setting aside the award which was dismissed on 11.07.2002 on contest. In spite of recording 0.20 acres under suit Plot No.1419 as gupat in the name of Bangladesh government, the defendants by give up many land of their own made the gupat as motorable road for their ingress and egress. The defendants while about to complete a pucca house by breaking their old house which is 6 feet away from northern side of the suit road, the plaintiffs filed the instant false suit and as such they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 4. The defendant No.5 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegation made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land is a gupat type of land under khatian No.1 which is the land of government khas khatian No.1 and there exist a 13 feet 14 feet road over the suit land and since it has rightly been recorded as government gupat land no one have any right to claim title or to make any house therein and as such no one can get any injunction over there and as such he prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 18. In view of the above it appears that the suit land is Government road recorded in the name of Government of Khas Khatian No.1 which is admitted by both the parties in the suit. In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiffs shall have to prove his exclusive possession and prima-facie title over the suit land. But admittedly the suit land is Government road and the plaintiff has no possession. In the instant case the plaintiffs having been prayed for permanent injunction with a view restraining the defendants not to construct Pucca house in the Government road which is obstruction of the plaintiffs for enjoyment of their movement from his dwelling house.
